title: Galatians Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Galatians 3: the Spirit received by hearing of faith, Abraham's blessing, the law as a tutor, and all being one in Christ Jesus.

questions.text: How does the chapter address the readers in its first verse?
questions.explanation: It opens by calling them foolish Galatians and asking who has bewitched them not to obey the truth.

answers.text: Beloved brothers
Children of promise
Foolish Galatians
Saints and faithful ones

questions.text: What did the writer want to learn about how they received the Spirit?
questions.explanation: He asks whether they received the Spirit by the works of the law, or by hearing of faith.

answers.text: Whether before or after they were taught
Whether by the works of the law or by hearing of faith
Whether through signs or through suffering
Whether from him or from another teacher

questions.text: What is said about Abraham in this chapter?
questions.explanation: It says that Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.

answers.text: He believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness
He kept the whole law from his youth up
He was given the law long before the promise
He offered gifts to God for his own sins

questions.text: What did the Scripture preach beforehand to Abraham?
questions.explanation: Foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, the Scripture preached beforehand to Abraham that in him all the nations will be blessed.

answers.text: That his offspring would be many
That the law would come to him
That his sons would rule the nations
That in him all the nations will be blessed

questions.text: What does the chapter say Christ redeemed us from?
questions.explanation: It says Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us.

answers.text: From the hands of our enemies
From the days and seasons
From the curse of the law
From the promise given to Abraham

questions.text: How long after the covenant does the chapter say the law came?
questions.explanation: It says the law came four hundred thirty years after the covenant that was confirmed beforehand by God, and does not annul it.

answers.text: Four hundred thirty years after
Forty years after
Four hundred years after
Four thousand years after

questions.text: Why does the chapter say the law was added?
questions.explanation: It says the law was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise has been made.

answers.text: To give Israel a mediator
Because of transgressions
To make the promise sure
To give life to the dead

questions.text: What has the law become, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: It says the law has become our tutor to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

answers.text: A seal of the promise
A witness against the Gentiles
A yoke that cannot be carried
Our tutor to bring us to Christ

questions.text: What does the chapter say about those who were baptized into Christ?
questions.explanation: It says that as many as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

answers.text: They have kept the whole law
They are still under a tutor
They have put on Christ
They have received the law of Moses

questions.text: What distinctions does the chapter say no longer stand in Christ Jesus?
questions.explanation: It says there is neither Jew nor Greek, neither slave nor free man, neither male nor female, for all are one in Christ Jesus.

answers.text: Jew and Greek, slave and free, male and female
Rich and poor, young and old
Teacher and pupil, strong and weak
Priest and people, near and far
